source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)
method: Consonantal analysis — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided

verses.translation: And afterward, Yeshua revealed [himself] to the other seventy-three disciples, and sent them two [by] two ahead of him into every place that he was about [or: prepared, destined] to come.

translation_notes: ואחר (אחר): Candidates: H309 'to loiter', H310 'after', H311 'after (Aramaic)', H312 'other/next', H313 'Acher'. Chose H310 because it functions as a temporal adverb 'and after/afterward' connecting to the next narrative event.

הראה (ראה): Candidates: H7200 'to see/show', H7201 'bird of prey', H7202 'seeing/experiencing', H7203 'seer/vision', H7204 'Roeh'. The ה prefix with causative sense gives 'he showed/revealed'. Chose H7200 as the verb 'to show' in hiphil-like usage.
אל: Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'mighty/God', H411 'these', H413 'to/near'. Chose H413 because the directional preposition 'to the others' is the only coherent reading here.
עתיד: Candidates: H6263 'prepared', H6264 'prepared/the future'. Chose H6264 because 'prepared/about to' fits the sense of future intention before the infinitive 'to come'.
textual_notes: ש(ים — the text has a damaged/parenthetical character. The reading שבעים (seventy) is reconstructed from context (sending disciples in pairs). The parenthetical mark suggests textual damage at this point.
הראה could be parsed as 'the seeing/vision' (noun) or as a hiphil verb 'he showed/caused to see'. The narrative context with Yeshua as subject favors the verbal reading.

verses.literal: And after, showed Yeshua to the others, seventy and three disciples, and sent-them two two before-him in all the places that he [was] about to come.

verses.translation: And he said: The yields [or: produce, increase] of the harvest [are] abundant, but the reapers [are] few. And he said to them: Say, Our Father, your name will be made holy [or: sanctified, set apart], and into your kingdom we will enter.

translation_notes: ואמר (אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because this is clearly a narrative verb 'and he said'.
רק: Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely/but', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H7535 because 'but/only' serves as a contrastive conjunction between 'many yields' and 'few reapers'.
להם: The ל prefix + הם. Candidates for הם: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 'to them' as the indirect object of 'he said'.

verses.literal: And he-said: yields of-the-harvest [are] many, only the-reapers [are] few. And he-said to-them: say, Our-Father, your-name will-be sanctified, and in-your-kingdom we-will-come.

verses.translation: Go! Look — I [am] sending you out like lambs [or: young sheep] among wolves. Give to us our allotted bread [or: food, sustenance] day [by] day.

translation_notes: הנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because 'behold' naturally introduces a dramatic declaration ('I am sending you...').
אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because the first person pronoun is required by the verb 'sending you'.
בין: Candidates: H995 'to understand', H996 'between/among', H997 'between (Aramaic)'. Chose H996 because 'among wolves' creates the coherent image of lambs surrounded by predators.

תן: The candidate H8565 'a monster/sea-serpent/jackal' is listed, but the consonants תן here clearly function as the imperative of נתן (H5414 'to give'). The Strong's entry H8565 refers to the noun תנין. Chose the imperative of H5414 as this begins a prayer petition 'give to us'.
לחם: Candidates: H3898 'to feed on/to battle', H3899 'bread/food', H3900 'bread (Aramaic)', H3901 'battle'. Chose H3899 because 'bread' is the natural object of 'give to us' in a prayer context.
textual_notes: לכו — the candidate listed is H3551 כו 'a window', but the consonants לכו are the standard imperative plural of הלך (H3212) 'go/walk'. The Strong's entry for כו is irrelevant here.

כשיות — not in the candidate list as a full form. The כ is a preposition 'as/like' and שיות appears to be the plural of שה (H7716) 'a lamb/sheep', giving 'as lambs'. The form is unusual but contextually clear.
חוקינו — 'our portion/statute'. This could derive from חק (H2706) 'statute/allotment/portion'. The sense 'our allotted portion' fits the prayer context of daily bread.

verses.literal: Go! Behold I [am] sending you as lambs among wolves. Give to-us bread [of] our-portion day day.

verses.translation: Do not carry a sack or a [money]stone [or: purse], nor leg-coverings [or: stockings], nor sandals, and do not give a greeting [or: peace, shalom] to any person on the road. And forgive [or: release, let go] to us all our sins, for we [are] forgiving [or: releasing] them to all who are indebted to us, and do not bring us into trial [or: testing, temptation].
words: our debtors / those obligated to us

translation_notes: שק: Candidates: H8242 'sack/sackcloth (mesh material)', H8243 'the leg'. Chose H8242 because 'do not carry a sack' fits the travel-light instruction; legs are not something one carries.

ואבן: Candidates: H68 'a stone', H69 'a stone (Aramaic)', H70 'pair of stones / potter's wheel'. Chose H68; 'stone' here likely refers to a money-weight or purse-stone, a common metonym for money/purse in the context of travel provisions.
ואל (first): Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative)', H410 'God/mighty', H413 'to'. Chose H408 because paired with the imperfect תתנו it forms a prohibitive 'do not give'.
שלום: Candidates: H7965 'peace/welfare/greeting', H7966 'requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum'. Chose H7965 because 'do not give a peace-greeting to anyone on the road' fits the urgency instruction.

לשום: Candidates: H7760 'to put/place/appoint', H7761 'to put (Aramaic)', H7762 'garlic'. Here לשום functions as 'to any' (ל + שום in the sense of 'any/whatever'). Chose H7760 used idiomatically as an indefinite pronoun.
אדם: Candidates: H119 'to be ruddy', H120 'a human being', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because 'any person' is the natural complement to the prohibition.
בדרך: Candidates: H1869 'to tread', H1870 'a road/way'. Chose H1870 because 'on the road' completes the travel scenario.

והנח: The candidate H5146 'Noah' is listed, but the consonants והנח clearly represent a verb form from נוח (H5117) 'to rest/release/set down' in hiphil imperative with ו-conjunction: 'and release/forgive'. This begins the prayer section.
ואל (second): Same as first — H408, prohibitive 'do not'.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'for/because/that'. Chose H3588 as the causal conjunction linking forgiveness given and received.
textual_notes: שוקים — the candidates listed (H7009-H7011) refer to קים roots. But שוקים most naturally derives from שוק (H7785) 'leg/thigh'. בתי שוקים = 'houses of legs' i.e. leg-coverings or stockings. This is an unusual compound but coherent in a list of travel garments.

ואבן — 'stone' is unexpected in a list of travel items. It may refer to a money-weight stone used as currency, or possibly an error/variant for another word. The reading 'purse-stone' (weight for commerce) fits the prohibition against carrying provisions.

והנח — there is a clear seam in this text where travel instructions transition into prayer language. The prayer section (forgive us... do not bring us into trial) appears embedded within the larger discourse.

verses.literal: Not you-will-carry sack and stone and not leg-coverings and not sandals and not you-will-give peace to-any man on-the-road. And release to-us all our-sins for we [are] releasing them to-all our-debtors and not bring-us to-trial.

verses.translation: And in whatever house you enter, you shall say first: Peace [or: wholeness, well-being] will come upon this house. And he said to them: Which among you has a friend, and goes to him at midnight, and says to him: My beloved [or: dear friend], lend me three loaves of bread.

translation_notes: ובבית: Candidates: H1004 'house', H1005 'house (Aramaic)', H1006 'Bajith'. Chose H1004 as the common noun 'house' with prepositions וב.

הזה: Candidate H1957 'to dream' vs. ה + זה H2088 'this'. Chose the demonstrative article + pronoun 'this' because 'this house' is contextually coherent, whereas 'to dream' produces no sensible reading.

אי: Candidates: H335 'where/how', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'howler/wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Chose H335 because אי זה together = 'which one' (interrogative), fitting the question 'which of you has a friend?'
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 as part of the interrogative phrase אי זה 'which?'
בחצי: Candidates: H2677 'the half/middle', H2678 'an arrow'. Chose H2677 because 'in the middle of the night' (midnight) is the natural setting for this parable.
הלוה (לוה): H3867 'to twine/unite/borrow/lend'. In hiphil the sense is 'lend'. Chose this because 'lend me' is the request being made.
ככרות: The candidate listed is H7327 'Ruth'. But ככרות is the construct plural of ככר (H3603) 'a round/loaf/talent'. Chose H3603 because 'loaves of bread' is the coherent reading.
לחם: Candidates: H3898 'to battle/consume', H3899 'bread/food', H3900 'bread (Aramaic)', H3901 'battle'. Chose H3899 as 'bread' completing 'loaves of bread'.
שלשה: Candidates: H8030 'Shilshah', H8031 'Shalishah', H7716 'sheep'. These don't fit. The consonants שלשה represent the number three (H7969). Chose 'three' as the quantity of loaves requested.
textual_notes: שתכנסו — no Strong's candidates provided. This is a relative clause שׁ + תכנסו from the root כנס 'to gather/enter', a later Hebrew verb form. It means 'that you enter into'.
ואמר — this shifts from instruction (peace upon this house) to a new parable. The narrative seam is clear from the switch to third person 'he said to them'.

verses.literal: And in-a-house that you-will-enter you-will-say first: peace will-come in-the-house the-this. And he-said to-them: which of-you has to-him a-friend and-he-goes to-him in-half the-night and-says to-him: my-beloved, lend to-me loaves [of] bread three.

verses.translation: And if there [is] a son of peace [or: a person worthy of peace], your peace will rest upon him. For my beloved [or: dear friend] has come to me from the road, and I have nothing [that] I am able to set before him.

translation_notes: ואם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because 'and if there is a son of peace' introduces a conditional clause.
שם: Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'name', H8035 'Shem', H8036 'name (Aramaic)'. Chose H8033 because 'if there [is] a son of peace' requires the existential adverb 'there'.
בן: Candidates: H1121 'son', H1122 'Ben (name)', H1123 'son (Aramaic)'. Chose H1121 because 'son of peace' is a Semitic idiom for one characterized by peace.
ינוח: The candidate H3239 'Janoach (place name)' is listed, but ינוח is clearly a verb form from נוח (H5117) 'to rest', 3ms imperfect: 'will rest'. The place name makes no sense here.
מהדרך: Candidates for דרך: H1869 'to tread', H1870 'road/way'. Chose H1870 with מה prefix meaning 'from the road/journey'.
ואין: Candidates: H369 'non-entity/not', H370 'whence', H371 'is it not?'. Chose H369 as the negative existential 'and there is not'.
מה: Candidates: H4100 'what?/what!', H4101 same. Chose H4100 as the interrogative/relative 'what [I am able to set]'.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'for/because'. Chose H3588 as the causal conjunction explaining why the request is being made.
textual_notes: ה(לום — the text has a damaged/parenthetical character again. The reading השלום (the peace) or הש(לום is reconstructed. The phrase בן השלום 'son of peace' is a well-known Semitic idiom.

2אוכל — the numeral 2 before אוכל appears to be a scribal mark or textual note, not part of the word. The root is יכל (H3201) 'to be able' in 1cs participle/imperfect form, or possibly אכל 'to eat/feed'. Context favors 'I am able' since it governs the infinitive להניח 'to set/place'.
להניח could mean 'to set before' (from נוח hiphil 'to cause to rest/place') or 'to leave/release'. Here 'to set/place [food] before him' is the coherent image.

verses.literal: And if there [is] a son of peace upon-him will-rest your-peace. For my-beloved has-come from-the-road to-me and-there-is-not to-me what I-am-able to-set before-him.

verses.translation: In that very same house remain [or: stand firm] and eat and drink from those provisions that they give you, for the laborer [or: worker] is worthy to have his wages [or: reward]. Do not desire [or: consent] to move from house to house

translation_notes: כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'because/for'. Introducing a reason for the instruction, H3588 'for/because' is clearly correct.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1933 'to be'. As a pronoun in a nominal clause ('worthy is he the worker'), H1931 fits.
אל: Candidates: H408 'do not (deprecative negation)', H410 'God/mighty', H413 'to/toward'. Before an imperfect verb תאבו, H408 'do not' is the standard negative volitive.
בית: Candidates: H1004 'house', H1006 'Bajith (place)'. Context of dwelling instructions makes H1004 obvious.
לעבור: Candidates: H5668 'on account of/transit', H5669 'stored grain'. With ל prefix as infinitive, this is from עבר 'to cross/pass over', meaning 'to move [from house to house]'.
textual_notes: ראוי is a late/Mishnaic Hebrew adjective meaning 'worthy/fitting' — not found as a standard Strong's entry. Root ראה 'to see' in its extended sense.
הפועל 'the worker/laborer' is from the root פעל 'to do/make' (H6466). The noun form פועל (H6467) means 'work/deed' but also 'worker'. This is standard Mishnaic Hebrew usage.
תאבו from root אבה (H14) 'to be willing/consent/desire'. The negation אל תאבו = 'do not be willing / do not consent'.

verses.literal: In that house itself stand and eat and drink from those things that they will give to you for worthy [is] he the worker to be to him his wages do not desire to pass from house to house

verses.translation: And in whatever city you enter where they welcome [or: receive] you, eat from those provisions [or: things] that are set [or: placed] before you

translation_notes: ובאי: Candidates for אי: H335 'where?', H336 'not', H339 'island/coast'. With prefix ו+ב and followed by זו, this reads 'and in which(ever)' — H335 'where/which' fits as an interrogative/relative pronoun.
זו: Candidates: H2097/H2098 'this/that', H2099 'Ziv (month)'. As a demonstrative relative ('whichever'), H2097 fits.
עיר: Candidates: H5892 'city', H5895 'donkey-colt'. Context of entering and being received clearly indicates H5892 'city'.

verses.literal: And in whichever city that you enter and they receive you eat from those things [that are] placed before you

verses.translation: And heal the sick [or: afflicted] who are there, and say to them: The kingdom [or: reign, dominion] of God is drawing near to you

translation_notes: שמה: Candidates: H8047 'ruin/desolation', H8048 'Shammah (name)', or the common adverb שמה 'there/thither' (H8033 with directional ה). Context of 'the sick who will be there' clearly points to 'there' as an adverb of place.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to burn/rankle', H1992 'they/them'. With ל prefix as 'to them', this is the prepositional phrase using the 3mp pronoun — H1992 is the base pronoun.
האל: Candidates: H408 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411 'these/those', H413 'to/toward'. With the article ה and following 'kingdom of', H410 'God/the Mighty One' is the only coherent reading.
מלכות: Candidates: H4438 'kingdom/dominion', H3575 'Cuth (Assyrian province)'. Paired with 'God', H4438 'kingdom' is obvious.
textual_notes: שמה as 'there' is technically a different vocalization than שמה 'desolation' (H8047). The consonants are identical. Context decisively favors 'there'.

verses.literal: And heal the sick that will be there and say to them [the] kingdom of God draws near to you

verses.translation: And if you enter into a city where they do not receive [or: welcome] you, go out into its open streets [or: public squares] and say

translation_notes: ואם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Opening a conditional clause, H518 'if' is correct.
בעיר: Candidates: H1165 'cattle', H5892 'city'. Following 'if you enter in', H5892 'city' produces the coherent image; H1165 'cattle' is nonsensical here.

verses.literal: And if you enter in a city that not they receive you go out in the streets and say

verses.translation: Even the dust that has collected [or: clung] to us, we shake off [or: remove] to give [back] to you. Only know this: that the kingdom [or: dominion] of God is drawing near

translation_notes: העפר: Candidates: H6080 'to be dust', H6081 'Epher (name)', H6082 'fawn', H6083 'dust/earth'. With the article ה, this is the noun H6083 'dust' — the image of shaking dust off one's feet.
רק: Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely/but', H7536 'spittle'. As a limiting adverb before 'know', H7535 'only/but' is the natural reading.
האל: Same as section 6 — H410 'God'.
textual_notes: שנאסף: Root אסף 'to gather/collect' (H622). With the prefix ש (relative 'that/which') and נ (nifal passive), this reads 'that was gathered/collected'. The image is of dust that has accumulated on the travelers.

מסירים: Root סור 'to turn aside/remove' (H5493) in hifil participle form with מ prefix. This means 'removing/taking away'. Alternatively from מסר 'to deliver/hand over' but the image of removing dust favors סור.

verses.literal: Also the dust that was gathered on us we [are] removing to give it to you only know that [the] kingdom of God draws near

verses.translation: And I say to you that on that day, Sodom and Gomorrah will not suffer [or: endure] evil comparable to [or: resembling] what you yourselves will endure

translation_notes: ואומר: The candidate H201 'Omar (grandson of Esau)' is a proper noun. However, the consonants אומר are the active participle of אמר 'to say' (H559). With the prefix ו, this is 'and [I am] saying' — a participial present tense. H559 is the root.
אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'a ship/fleet'. Following 'and I say', H589 'I' is the pronoun.
רע: Candidates: H7451 'evil/bad', H7452 'crash/noise', H7453 'associate/friend', H7455 'badness'. As the object of suffering, H7451 'evil' fits best.

כדומה: Candidates for דומה: H1745 'silence/death', H1746 'Dumah (place)'. However, the consonants כדומה can also be read as כ + דומה from root דמה 'to be like/resemble' (H1819). This yields 'like the likeness of' or 'comparable to', which fits the comparative context perfectly.
לאשר: Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/that', H835 'happiness'. With ל prefix introducing what they will endure, H834 'that which/what' is correct.
אתם: H864 'Etham (place)' is the only candidate provided, but these consonants are clearly the 2mp independent pronoun 'you' (H859 in its plural form). Context demands the pronoun.
textual_notes: The sentence structure is ambiguous: it could mean (a) Sodom and Gomorrah will not endure evil comparable to what you endure (i.e., your punishment is worse), or (b) less likely, Sodom and Gomorrah did not suffer evil like what you will endure. The imperfect יסבלו suggests future, supporting reading (a).

כדומה: If from דומה H1745 'silence/death', it would read 'like death/silence' — but this doesn't connect well with the following לאשר. Reading it as 'comparable to / like the likeness of' from דמה 'to resemble' is more coherent.

verses.literal: And saying I to you that in that day not will endure Sodom and Gomorrah evil like the likeness of that which you will endure it you

verses.translation: Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Beth-Tsidah [house of Sidon/provision]! For if in Tyre or in Sodom the mighty works [or: signs, miracles] that were performed in you had been performed, [clothed] in sackcloth and [sitting] in ashes, prostrated [or: humbled], they would have been making repentance [or: turning back]

translation_notes: אוי: Candidates: H188 'woe/lamentation', H189 'Evi (Midianite chief)'. As an interjection of lamentation, H188 is correct.
בית: Candidates: H1004 'house', H1006 'Bajith'. As part of the place name 'Beth-Tsidah', H1004 'house of' is the standard construct.

צידה: H6720 'food/provision'. However, the consonants צידה also align with the place name Tsidah/Sidon (cf. H6721 Tsidon). Given the pairing with Tyre (Tsor) in the next line, this likely refers to Beth-Saida (Bethsaida), rendered here as 'house of Tsidah/provision/fishing'.
כי: H3588 'for/because' introducing the reason for the woe.

בצור: Candidates: H1208 'inaccessible/lofty', H6696 'to cramp/confine', H6697 'rock/cliff', H6698 'Tsur (name)'. In parallel with Sodom as a city, this is Tyre (צור), the famous Phoenician city — H6697/H6698.
או: H176 'or' — connecting Tyre and Sodom as alternatives.

לאחור: H268 'the hinder part/backward'. However, in context of mourning alongside ashes, this likely represents a word for sackcloth. The consonants could potentially be read differently, but H268 is the provided candidate. This may be a scribal variant or the translator's rendering of 'sackcloth' using a term meaning 'rough back-covering'. Alternatively, this is שק (sackcloth) rendered unusually.
ובאפר: Candidates: H665 'ashes', H666 'turban'. Paired with mourning imagery, H665 'ashes' is correct.
תשובה: H8666 'a return/recurrence/reply'. In religious context, this means 'repentance' (turning back to God) — standard later Hebrew usage.
textual_notes: צידה could be the common noun 'food/provision' (H6720) or a form of the place name Sidon/Bethsaida. Context strongly suggests the place name Bethsaida (בית צידה), a town associated with Jesus's ministry.

לאחור (H268 'backward/behind') is unexpected in a mourning context where one expects 'sackcloth' (שק). This may be the manuscript's idiosyncratic rendering or a corruption. The pairing with 'ashes' strongly suggests mourning garb was intended. It could also be read as a separate word — 'long ago' (i.e., 'they would have repented long ago in ashes').
The brackets around אם suggest a scribal or editorial insertion, indicating uncertainty about whether the conditional particle was in the original.
בצור: While H6697 'rock' is the base meaning, in a geographical list with Sodom, this almost certainly refers to Tyre (the Phoenician city). The same consonants serve for both.
נסים: Not provided with Strong's candidates. Root נס (H5251 'banner/sign') or the later Hebrew meaning 'miracles'. In context of mighty deeds performed, 'miracles/signs' is intended.

verses.literal: Woe to you Chorazin woe to you house [of] Tsidon for if in Tsor or in Sodom would be done signs that were done in you in sackcloth and in ashes prostrated they would be doing repentance

verses.translation: Truly, the evil [or: calamity] of Tyre and Sodom will not compare to the evil [or: destruction, breakage] that is prepared for you on the day of the judgment.
words: comparable / resembling (from root דמה, silence used figuratively)

translation_notes: רע (consonants רע): Candidates: H7451 'evil', H7452 'crash/noise', H7453 'associate', H7454 'thought', H7455 'badness'. Chose H7451 because the context is about punishment/judgment prepared for a day of reckoning, and 'evil/calamity' fits the comparison between cities.

צור (consonants צור): Candidates: H6696 'to cramp/confine', H6697 'rock/cliff', H6698 'Tsur (personal name)'. Chose H6697 as a place name — Tyre is called צור (the rock city), and paired with Sodom it clearly refers to the famous city.

דומה (consonants דומה): Candidates: H1745 'silence/death', H1746 'Dumah (place)'. Neither is a perfect match; the form more likely derives from the root דמה (to be like/compare), functioning as an adjective 'comparable/similar.' H1745 shares consonants but 'silence' doesn't fit the syntax; the verb דמה (to resemble) is the contextual fit.

לרעה (consonants רעה): Candidates: H7462 'to shepherd/tend', H7463 'male companion', H7464 'female associate', H7465 'breakage'. Chose H7465 because the preposition ל + רעה in context of judgment means 'to the evil/destruction' — breakage/calamity fits the punishment theme.

הדין (consonants דין): Candidates: H1777 'sail direct', H1778 'to judge', H1779 'judgment', H1780 'judgment', H1781 'judge', H1782 'judge'. Chose H1779 because 'the judgment' (noun with article ה) is what fits 'day of the judgment.'
textual_notes: דומה could be parsed as H1745 'silence/death' (Dumah), but contextually it functions as a comparative adjective from the root דמה 'to resemble.' The manuscript may be using a form of דמה rather than the noun דומה.

לרעה could be parsed as 'to the shepherding' (H7462) or 'to the female companion' (H7464), but in context of judgment and punishment, 'to the evil/calamity' (from רעה as feminine of רע) is the coherent reading.

verses.literal: Verily not will-be [the] evil [of] Tyre and Sodom comparable to-the-evil the-prepared for-you for-[the]-day [of] the-judgment

verses.translation: And you, Kfar Nachum [Village of Comfort], will you exalt yourself up to the heart [or: midst] of the heavens? For into the depths of Gehinnom you will descend.
words: you will be lifted up (2fs imperfect hitpael/nifal of נשא)
you will descend (2fs imperfect qal of ירד)

translation_notes: ואת (consonants את): Candidates: H852 'portent', H853 'direct object marker', H854 'nearness/with', H855 'hoe'. חפץ (consonants חפץ): Candidates: H2654 'to incline to/desire/be pleased', H2655 'pleased with', H2656 'pleasure/desire'. Chose H2654 because the verbal form 'desired/wanted' fits the narrative: he wanted to justify himself.

לצדק (consonants צדק): Candidates: H6663 'to be/make right (causatively)', H6664 'righteousness'. Chose H6663 because ל + infinitive construct of the causative 'to justify' makes grammatical sense with 'himself' as object.
ואמר: Chose H559 — 'and said.'
לישוע: Chose H3442 — 'to Yeshua.'
ומי (consonants מי): H4310 'who?' — the only candidate, and fits as an interrogative.
הוא: Chose H1931 'he/is he' — copulative use in a question.

חברי: The listed candidate H2277 'Chebrite' (descendants of Cheber) is a gentilicname. However, the consonants חבר + י clearly represent חבר 'companion/associate/friend' (H2270) with 1st person possessive suffix 'my companion.' The context demands this reading.
textual_notes: חברי could theoretically refer to 'Chebrite' (H2277) but contextually must be 'my companion/neighbor' from the root חבר with possessive suffix. The narrative is asking about the identity of one's fellow/neighbor.

verses.literal: And he desired to justify himself and said to Yeshua and who [is] he my companion

verses.translation: And Yeshua, looking at him, said: A certain man [was] going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among thieves [or: robbers], and they stripped him and struck him [with] striking [that left] wounds [or: bruises], and they went away and left him as [one] dead

translation_notes: אדם (consonants אדם): Candidates: H119 'to be ruddy', H120 'a human being/man', H121 'Adam', H122 'rosy', H123 'Edom', H124 'ruby'. Chose H120 because the narrative introduces a generic human character, 'a man.'
אחד (consonants אחד): Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/a certain'. Chose H259 — indefinite article 'a certain [man].'
בין (consonants בין): Candidates: H995 'to understand', H996 'between/among', H997 Aramaic same. Chose H996 'among' because the man fell among thieves.
להם (consonants להם/הם): Candidates: H3859 'to rankle', H1990 'Ham', H1991 'wealth', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 — the prepositional phrase 'to themselves' (i.e., they went away).

כמת (consonants מת): H4962 'an adult/man.' However, the consonants כ + מת more naturally read as כ 'as/like' + מת 'dead (one)' from H4191 (the adjective/participle 'dead'). The context describes leaving someone appearing dead.
הכאת: Parsed as noun construct form of הכאה 'striking/blow' — a verbal noun from נכה 'to strike.'
והניחשהו: Parsed as 'and they left him' — likely from נוח/נחש but in context means 'they abandoned/left him.' The form appears unusual and may contain a scribal variant.
textual_notes: והניחשהו is morphologically unusual. It could be from נוח (Hiphil: 'to set down, leave') with an extra ש, possibly a scribal error or dialectal form. The meaning 'and they left him' is clear from context.
ביריחו with the prefix ב could mean 'in Jericho' or could indicate direction 'toward Jericho' — the narrative clearly means traveling toward Jericho.
כמת: The only listed candidate is H4962 'an adult male,' but the phrase clearly means 'as dead/like a dead [person]' from the root מות.

verses.literal: And Yeshua looking-at-him said a man one going-down from Jerusalem to-Jericho and came among thieves and they stripped him and struck him striking of wounds and went to themselves and left him as dead

verses.translation: And it happened that a certain priest [was] walking on that same road, and he saw him and passed on [to the far side]

translation_notes: וקרא (consonants קרא): Candidates: H7121 'to call out', H7122 'to encounter/happen upon', H7123 Aramaic 'to call', H7124 'partridge'. Chose H7122 because 'and it happened/it chanced' introduces a coincidental event in the narrative.

שכהן (consonants כהן): Candidates: H3547 'to officiate as priest', H3548 'a priest', H3549 Aramaic 'priest'; also הן candidates H2004-H2006. Chose H3548 because ש + כהן = 'that a priest,' using the relative particle ש with the noun 'priest.'
אחד: Chose H259 'one/a certain.'
דרך (consonants דרך): Candidates: H1869 'to tread', H1870 'a road/way'. Chose H1870 because this is a noun: 'that same road.'
וראה (consonants ראה): Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7202 'seeing/experiencing', H7203 'seer/vision', H7204 'Roeh'. Chose H7200 — the verb 'and he saw.'
ועבר (consonants עבר): Candidates: H5674 'to cross over/pass by', H5675-H5677 noun/name forms. Chose H5674 — the verb 'and he passed by.'

הלאה (consonants הלאה): Candidates: H1973 'to the distance/far away', H3811 'to tire', H3812 'Leah'. Chose H1973 because 'and passed onward/to the far side' describes the priest avoiding the wounded man.
textual_notes: וקרא could be 'and he called' (H7121) or 'and it happened/chanced' (H7122). The narrative flow favors H7122 — an incidental encounter is being described.

verses.literal: And it happened that a priest one walking in that road itself and saw him and passed onward

verses.translation: And a certain Levite [came] near to that place, and behold he [too was] passing from [there] and onward [or: beyond]

translation_notes: ולוי (consonants לוי): Candidates: H3878 'Levi', H3879 'a wreath'. Chose H3878 — 'a Levite,' the tribal designation, consistent with the narrative of temple functionaries.
אחד: Chose H259 'one/a certain.'
מקום (consonants מקום/קום): Candidates: H4725 'a place/standing', H6965 'to rise', H6966 Aramaic 'to rise'. Chose H4725 because the noun 'place' fits — 'near that place.'
והנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither', H2009 'lo!/behold', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 — 'and behold' introduces the observation of his passing by.
הוא: Chose H1931 'he' — emphatic pronoun.
והלאה: Candidates: H1973 'to the distance/onward', H3811 'to tire', H3812 'Leah'. Chose H1973 — 'and onward/beyond,' same as section 8.
textual_notes: מ<ם appears to contain a damaged or illegible character (<). The most likely reading is משם 'from there,' with the ש partially corrupted. The מ preposition + שם 'there' = 'from there' fits the context of passing away from the location.
The syntax is somewhat compressed — 'a Levite one near from that place' likely means 'a certain Levite [came/drew] near to that place' or 'being near that place.'

verses.literal: And a Levite one near from that place and behold he passing from [there] and onward

verses.translation: But a certain Samaritan, passing near him, came to him and saw him and had compassion [or: showed mercy, pitied] upon him

translation_notes: אחד: Chose H259 'one/a certain.'
קרוב: H7138 'near' — the only candidate, describing the Samaritan's proximity.
וראה (consonants ראה): Candidates: H7200 'to see', H7201 'vulture', H7202 'seeing', H7203 'seer', H7204 'Roeh'. Chose H7200 — 'and he saw,' the natural verb for perceiving the wounded man.
וחמל: H2550 'to commiserate/spare/show compassion' — the only candidate and perfectly fits the narrative: the Samaritan, unlike the priest and Levite, responded with compassion.
textual_notes: ושמרוני is a gentilic form from שמרון (Samaria/Shomron). No Strong's number is provided in the candidates but the form clearly means 'a Samaritan' — one from Samaria.

verses.literal: And a Samaritan one passing near from him came to him and saw him and had-compassion on him

verses.translation: And he applied [or: poured] oil on his wounds, and bound them up, and brought him to the inn [ushpiza], and set [or: kept] his eyes upon him [watching over him attentively]

translation_notes: ושם (שם): Candidates: H8033 'there/then', H8034 'name/appellation', H8035 'Shem', H8036 'name (Aramaic)'. However, with waw-consecutive and the verb שים (to put/place/set), the consonants ושם can also represent ויָשֶׂם (and he placed). In context — placing oil on wounds — this is clearly the verb 'to put/place' (שים, H7760, though not listed among candidates, the consonantal form ושם with prefix waw fits שים perfectly). The alternative readings 'and there' or 'and a name' produce incoherent images before 'for him oil on his wounds.' Chose the verbal reading 'and he placed.'

שמן: Candidates: H8080 'to be oily', H8081 'oil/grease', H8082 'greasy/rich'. The noun 'oil' (H8081) fits perfectly as the object being placed on wounds — a standard ancient healing practice. The verb or adjective readings make no sense as a direct object here.

ונתן (נתן): Candidates: H5414 'to give/put', H5415 'give (Aramaic)', H5416 'Nathan (proper name)'. As a verb with waw-consecutive 'and he gave/set,' this fits the idiom נתן עיניו בו ('set his eyes on him' = watched over him). The proper name Nathan makes no sense here.
textual_notes: ושם could theoretically be parsed as 'and there' (H8033) rather than 'and he placed' (from שים). Context strongly favors the verbal reading since 'and there for him oil on his wounds' is syntactically awkward, while 'and he placed for him oil on his wounds' is natural.

באושפיזא is an Aramaic loanword (from Greek ξενοδοχεῖον via Aramaic אושפיזא) meaning 'inn/lodging house.' It has no Strong's number as it is not a biblical Hebrew word but appears in later Hebrew/Aramaic texts.

verses.literal: And he placed for him oil on his wounds and bandaged him and brought him to [the] inn and gave his eyes on him

verses.translation: And on the next day, he took two peshitin [coins] and gave them to the innkeeper, and said to him: Provide for this wounded man all [of] his needs. And if you spend on his behalf more than these peshitin [coins], I will give [the remainder] to you upon my return.

translation_notes: לקח: Candidates: H3947 'to take', H3948 'instruction/teaching'. In context of taking coins, H3947 'to take' is clearly correct.
שני: Candidates: H8144 'crimson', H8145 'two/second'. Before a noun denoting coins (פשיטין), 'two' (H8145) is the natural reading. 'Crimson peshitin' would be bizarre.
ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. With waw-consecutive introducing direct speech, H559 'to say' is the only viable reading.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Demonstrative pronoun 'this' pointing to the wounded man. 'A sheep' makes no contextual sense.
ואם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. After the imperative clause, a conditional 'and if' (H518) introducing a further stipulation is the natural reading. 'And mother' is nonsensical.

אלו: Candidates: H431 'lo!/behold', H432 'if/nay'. In post-biblical Hebrew, אלו functions as a demonstrative pronoun 'these.' This fits the context: 'these peshitin.' Both Strong's entries are less fitting, but H431 as a deictic particle is closest.
textual_notes: פשיטין is an Aramaic/post-biblical Hebrew term for small coins (from פשט, to extend/spread — flat coins). No Strong's number applies.
למוכה — from the root נכה (to strike/smite), the passive participle מוכה means 'one who is struck/wounded.' No Strong's candidate was provided; this is a standard participial form.

מ<ני — the text appears to have a lacuna or uncertain letter (marked with <). This likely reads מני or מן meaning 'than/from,' a partitive preposition. The damaged character makes certainty impossible.

בחזרתו — 'in his return.' The suffix could refer to the speaker ('my return') or a third party. Context of the narrative (the one leaving promising to return) suggests it means 'upon my return,' though the consonantal suffix -ו is third person. This may reflect a narrative style where the speaker refers to himself in third person, or it could be an error.

יתנם — 'he will give them.' The subject is ambiguous: is it the speaker promising 'I will give' (in which case we'd expect אתנם) or a third-person reference? Likely the speaker referring to himself, parallel to the third-person suffix on בחזרתו.

verses.literal: And on the morrow he took two peshitin and gave them to the innkeeper and said to him do for [the] stricken-one this all [of] his need and if you spend in his expenses more than these peshitin these he will give them to him in his return

verses.translation: Which one of these three seems to you to have been more [of] a companion [or: neighbor, associate] and friend [or: fellow] to the one who fell among the robbers?

translation_notes: אי: Candidates: H335 'where/how/which', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island/coast'. Combined with זה, אי זה forms the interrogative 'which?' (literally 'where this?'). This is a standard Hebrew idiom. H335 is correct.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Part of the interrogative compound אי זה 'which one.' H2088 is correct.

מאלה: The מ prefix means 'from/of.' Candidates for אלה: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak', H425 'Elah', H426 'God'. However, אלה also serves as the common demonstrative pronoun 'these' (not listed among Strong's candidates here, but standard Hebrew אלה H428). In context — 'which of these three' — the demonstrative 'these' is the only coherent reading.
שהיה (היה): Candidates: H1961 'to exist/be/become', H1962 'ruin'. With the relative ש prefix, 'that he was' (H1961) is the natural reading. 'That ruin' makes no sense.

חבר: Candidates: H2266 'to join', H2267 'society/spell', H2268 'Cheber', H2269 'associate', H2270 'associate', H2271 'partner'. In context, paired with רע (friend), a noun meaning 'companion/associate' fits perfectly. H2270 'an associate' is chosen.

ורע: Candidates: H7451 'bad/evil', H7452 'crash/noise', H7453 'associate/friend', H7454 'thought', H7455 'badness'. Paired with חבר (companion), H7453 'friend/fellow' creates a natural hendiadys: 'companion and friend.' H7451 'evil' would produce the bizarre reading 'more companion and evil.'
שנפל (נפל): Candidates: H5307 'to fall', H5308 'to fall (Aramaic)', H5309 'abortion'. With relative ש prefix, 'who fell' (H5307) is the clear reading.

בין: Candidates: H995 'to understand', H996 'between/among', H997 'between (Aramaic)'. As a preposition before הגנבים (the thieves), 'among' (H996) is correct. 'To understand the thieves' would require different syntax.
textual_notes: ה<לשה — the text has a damaged or uncertain character (marked <). This almost certainly reads השלשה (the three), from שלש. The damaged letter would be ש.

מאלה — the demonstrative pronoun אלה ('these') is not among the Strong's candidates provided (which list H421-H426). The correct Strong's would be H428 (אלה, demonstrative 'these'). I have used H426 as a placeholder since it was the closest listed candidate, but the actual word is the demonstrative pronoun.
הגנבים — from גנב (H1590, thief/robber). The article ה plus plural form. Could mean thieves or robbers.

verses.literal: Which one from these the three appeared to you that he was more companion and friend to that one who fell among the thieves

verses.translation: And he said to him: The one who showed [or: did] him the faithful-kindness [chesed]. And Yeshua said to him: Go, and you do likewise.

translation_notes: ואמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say (Aramaic)', H561 'something said', H563 'lamb', H564 'Immer'. Waw-consecutive + verb introducing speech: H559 'and he said.'

החסד: Candidates: H2616 'to be kind', H2617 'kindness/piety', H2618 'Chesed (name)'. With the definite article ה, the noun 'the kindness' (H2617) fits perfectly — referring back to the specific act of mercy described. The verb or proper name would not take the article this way.

ההוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/that', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist (Aramaic)'. With the article ה prefix, this is the demonstrative 'that' (H1931), modifying החסד: 'that kindness.'
וישוע: Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua/Yeshua', H3443 'Jeshua'. This is the proper name Yeshua (Jesus). H3442 is the standard entry.
אמר (second occurrence): Same candidates as ואמר above. H559 'said.'

ואתה: Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 'to arrive (Aramaic)', H859 'you (pronoun)'. After the imperative לך (go), 'and you' (H859) as an emphatic subject pronoun before תעשה (you shall do) is the natural reading. 'And arrived' disrupts the imperative command structure.

כן: Candidates: H3651 'so/thus/likewise', H3652 'so (Aramaic)', H3653 'pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. As an adverb after תעשה (you shall do), 'thus/likewise' (H3651) completes the instruction perfectly. 'A gnat' or 'pedestal' would be absurd.

verses.literal: And he said to him the one who did for him the kindness that and Yeshua said to him go and you do thus

verses.translation: And it happened that while [they were] walking, he entered a certain village, and a woman whose name was Miriam [Mary] received him into her home. And the Pharisee said in his heart: Why does this [man] not wash his hands at the morning meal?

translation_notes: בעוד: H5750 'while/still' — temporal clause as in section 6.

במגדול: Candidates: H4024 'Migdol (place in Egypt),' H1419 'great.' However, in a narrative about entering a settlement, this likely represents a form related to מגדל 'tower' or, more likely in Mishnaic Hebrew, a village/settlement. The context of entering 'a certain [one]' with אחד suggests a generic settlement, not the Egyptian Migdol.
אחד: H259 'one/a certain' — modifying the village.

מה: H4100 'what' — but here used as part of the phrase שמה 'whose name,' with ש (relative) + מה functioning as a name introduction. The damaged text וא ה ש מה likely reads 'and a woman whose name [was].'
מרים: H4813 'Miriam' — a proper name.
אמר: Candidates include H559 'to say,' H561 'something said,' H563 'lamb,' H564 'Immer.' As a narrative verb of speech, H559 'said' is unmistakable.
למה: H4100 with ל prefix — 'why/for what reason.'
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that,' H2089 'sheep,' H2090 'this.' H2088 as demonstrative pronoun 'this one' fits the Pharisee pointing to the person.
הבקר: Candidates: H1239 'to inspect,' H1241 'cattle,' H1242 'morning.' In context of a meal time, H1242 'morning' is the natural reading — 'the morning meal.'
ונעשה: Root עשה with נ prefix — niphal 'it was done/it happened.' Common narrative transition.
שהולכים: ש (relative) + ה (article) + הולכים (walking, qal participle mp of הלך).
רוחץ: Qal participle of רחץ 'to wash.'
בסעודת: ב + סעודת (construct of סעודה 'meal/feast'). Post-biblical Hebrew.
textual_notes: במגדול: The text seems to intend 'village/town' but the candidates only offer H4024 'Migdol (Egypt)' or H1419 'great.' This may be a variant spelling of מגדל or a dialectal term for a small settlement/village.
The sequence וא ה ש מה appears to be damaged or fragmented text. Reconstructed as ואשה שמה 'and a woman whose name' — the spacing may reflect manuscript damage.
The section conflates two scenes: Mary receiving him (a hospitality scene) and the Pharisee commenting on hand-washing (a meal scene). This may represent a composite or condensed text.

verses.literal: And it happened while they [were] walking, he entered into a village one, and a woman whose name [was] Miriam received him into [the] midst of her house. And the Pharisee said in his heart, why this [one] is not washing his hands at [the] meal of the morning.

verses.translation: And there was a sister whose name was Marta [Martha], and [Mary was] sitting at the feet of Yeshua [Jesus] the Anointed One [Messiah], and she listened to his words. And our lord said to him: Pharisees! Now you purify what is on the outside of the cup and the bowl, but what is on the inside of you — it is an evil [or: wicked] heart and theft [or: robbery].

translation_notes: והיה: H1961 'to be/exist/become' with ו — 'and there was/it came to be.'
אחות: H269 'sister' — the only candidate and it fits: introducing Martha as Mary's sister.
ישוע: Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua,' H3443 same. Both refer to the same name. H3442 chosen as the primary entry.
משיח: Candidates: H4899 'anointed/Messiah,' H7878 'to ponder,' H7879 'utterance,' H7880 'shrub.' Following a personal name as a title, H4899 'Anointed One/Messiah' is the clear reading.

ושמעה: Candidates listed H8093/H8094 (names) and H4577-H4579 (bowels/belly). But this is clearly ו + שמעה, 3fs perfect of שמע 'to hear' — 'and she heard.' The candidate entries appear to misidentify the root.
אמר: H559 'to say' — narrative speech verb, as in previous sections.
מה (in questions): H4100 'what' — introducing the object of purification.
ומן: Candidates include H4478 'manna,' H4480 'from/out of.' As a preposition 'and from' connecting goblet and dish, H4480 is the clear reading.
רע: Candidates: H7451 'evil,' H7452 'noise,' H7453 'associate,' H7454 'thought,' H7455 'badness.' Modifying 'heart' in a moral critique, H7451 'evil' fits the condemnation of inner corruption.
בפנים: H6440 'face/front' — used adverbially with ב as 'inside/within.'
<הוא: The < indicates damaged text. Reading as שהוא (ש+הוא) 'that is' — a relative clause.
textual_notes: The text conflates the Martha/Mary scene with the Pharisee's criticism. The narrative shifts from describing Mary sitting at Yeshua's feet to addressing the Pharisee about purification. This may be a deliberate interweaving in the manuscript.
ש מה appears again as a fragmented form of שמה 'whose name.' The spacing suggests manuscript damage.
<הוא appears twice with a damaged initial letter. Reading as שהוא 'that is' based on the relative clause pattern ש+הוא.
אתם: The only candidate is H864 'Etham (a place),' but this is clearly the 2mp pronoun 'you.' The Strong's candidate list is incomplete for this common pronoun.

verses.literal: And there was a sister whose name [was] Marta, and sitting at [the] feet of Yeshua Mashiach, and she heard his words. And our lord said to him, Pharisees, now you [are] purifying what is from outside [the] goblet and from the dish, and what is on [the] inside of you, it [is] an evil heart and theft.

verses.translation: And Martha was busying herself [or: exerting herself] laboring over what was needed for him. Therefore she said to him: Tell him to help me! — Fools! Did not the one who made what is on the outside also make what is on the inside?

translation_notes: במה: Candidates: H1116 'elevation/high place,' H4100 'what.' With ב prefix, 'in what' (H4100) fits — describing what Martha labored over, i.e., what was needed.
כן: Candidates: H3651 'thus/therefore,' H3652 'so,' H3653 'stand,' H3654 'gnat.' With ל prefix, לכן = 'therefore' (H3651).
מי: H4310 'who' — introducing the rhetorical question about the Creator.
שעשה: ש (relative) + עשה (H6213 'to do/make'). 'Who made.'
מתחזקת: Hithpael participle fs of חזק 'to be strong' — reflexive 'exerting/busying herself.'
לטרוח: Infinitive construct of טרח 'to labor/toil' with ל prefix. Post-biblical Hebrew.
סכלים: Plural of סכל 'fool.' An exclamatory address.
תאמר: 3fs imperfect of אמר 'to say' — 'she says/will say.'
שיעזרני: ש (that) + י (3ms imperfect prefix) + עזר (help) + ני (me). 'That he would help me.'
textual_notes: The text appears to merge two different narrative threads: Martha's request for help (a domestic scene) and the 'Fools!' exclamation about inside/outside (a theological argument about purification). The paragraph mark (') may indicate a textual boundary between these two threads.

The question 'Did not the one who made the outside also make the inside?' shifts from domestic to theological/philosophical discourse. The antecedent of 'fools' is ambiguous — it could address the Pharisees (from the previous section's context) rather than Martha.

verses.literal: And Marta [was] exerting herself to labor in what [was] needed for him. Therefore she will say to him that he would help me. Fools! He who made what is from outside, did he not make what is on the inside?

verses.translation: And the Lord answered and said to her: Martha, Martha — you are found diligent [or: industrious, busy] in many matters [or: affairs, concerns]. Therefore, give in charity [or: righteousness, generosity] what is surplus [or: extra, remaining] to you, and all things will be pure [or: clean] for you.

translation_notes: וענה: Candidates: H6030 'to respond/answer,' H6031 'to depress/afflict,' H6034 'Anah (name).' As a narrative verb paired with 'said,' H6030 'answered' is the standard formula.
האדון: Candidates: H113 'sovereign/lord,' H114 'Addon (name).' With the article, H113 'the Lord' is the clear reading — referring to the speaker with authority.
ואמר: H559 'to say' — standard speech verb.
בצדקה: Candidates: H6665 'beneficence,' H6666 'righteousness/justice.' In context of giving surplus, H6666 captures both 'righteousness' and the Mishnaic sense of 'charity/almsgiving.'
לכן: H3651 'therefore' — as in previous sections.
חרוצה: From root חרץ 'to be sharp/diligent/decisive.' Feminine adjective: 'diligent/industrious.'
נמצאת: Niphal participle/perfect 2fs of מצא 'to find' — 'you are found/discovered.'
תנו: 2mp imperative of נתן 'to give.' The shift to plural suggests addressing the Pharisees (from context) or a broader audience.
<יותר: Damaged initial letter + יותר (H3148 'more/surplus'). Likely שיותר 'that is surplus/extra.'
טהורים: Plural adjective from טהר 'pure/clean.' 'Pure/clean things.'
textual_notes: The address shifts from singular 'Marta, Marta' (2fs) to plural 'give' (תנו) and 'to you' (לכם). This shift suggests the teaching pivots from Martha personally to a broader audience, likely the Pharisees from the earlier context.
בצדקה in Mishnaic Hebrew commonly means 'charity/almsgiving' rather than abstract 'righteousness.' Both senses may be intended here.
<יותר has a damaged initial character. Likely שיותר (ש+יותר) 'that is surplus/remaining,' functioning as a relative clause.

verses.literal: And answered the Lord and said to her, Marta Marta, diligent you are found in many matters. Therefore give in righteousness what is surplus to you, and all the things will be to you pure.

verses.translation: Truly, one thing is necessary. You, Miriam, have chosen the better [or: superior] portion — which will not be taken [or: robbed] from her. But only woe to you, Pharisees, for you tithe the mint and the rue and the cabbage [or: caraway], yet you abandon justice and the righteousness of YHWH. These are the things that are worthy to be done — and not to neglect them.

translation_notes: דבר (D-B-R): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a thing/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because 'one thing is needed' makes contextual sense as a statement about what is necessary.
אחד (ʾ-Ḥ-D): Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. Chose H259 because 'one thing' is natural with the noun דבר.

את (ʾ-T): Candidates: H852 'portent', H853 'object marker', H854 'with/near', H855 'hoe'. Here את functions as second-person feminine singular pronoun 'you' addressing Miriam, or as an object marker. Given the address to Miriam and the verb בחרת, it reads as 'you, Miriam, chose.' Both parsings yield similar meaning.

החלק (H-Ḥ-L-Q): Candidates: H2505 'to apportion', H2506 'portion/allotment', H2507 proper name, H2508 'part', H2509 'smooth', H2510 proper name. Chose H2506 because 'the portion' fits naturally with choosing the better part.
טוב (Ṭ-W-B): Candidates: H2895 'to be good', H2896 'good (adj)', H2897 place name, H2898 'goodness (noun)'. Chose H2896 because it serves as adjective modifying the portion.

אשר (ʾ-Š-R): Candidates: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/that', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 as the relative pronoun 'which' introducing the clause about what will not be taken.
אוי (ʾ-W-Y): Candidates: H188 'woe/lamentation', H189 'Evi (proper name)'. Chose H188 because 'woe to you' is a natural exclamatory address.

והכרוב (W-H-K-R-W-B): The Strong's candidates provided are H3742 'cherub' and H3743 'Kerub (place)'. However, in context of herbs being tithed (mint, rue, and ___), this must refer to a plant. The consonants כרוב also correspond to cabbage/caraway in later Hebrew usage. I read this as 'cabbage' (a garden plant), not 'cherub.'
textual_notes: את before מרים could be the object marker (H853) or the second-person feminine pronoun 'you.' Both yield essentially the same meaning: 'you, Miriam, chose' vs. 'Miriam chose.' The feminine verb form בחרת supports 'you chose.'

והכרוב: The only Strong's candidates are H3742 'cherub' and H3743 'Kerub (place),' but contextually among tithed herbs this must be a plant (cabbage or similar green). This is a post-biblical Hebrew usage not captured in Strong's.
The bracket markers ] [ in the source text suggest a textual break or section division between the Miriam passage and the woe oracle.

verses.literal: In truth one thing [is] needed. You Miriam chose the portion [that is] more good which not they will rob from her. But only woe to you Pharisees that you tithe the mint and the rue and the cabbage and abandon judgment and righteousness [of] YHWH. These [are] the things worthy that they should do and not to leave them.
